title: An element good with respect to a maximal regular sequence of a Cohen–Macaulay module is a nonzerodivisor
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (a Noetherian commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$). For a finite $R$-module $N$ let $\operatorname{Supp}(N)$ be the set of prime ideals $\mathfrak p\subset R$ with $N_{\mathfrak p}\neq0$, $N_{\mathfrak p}$ the localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], and let $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(N)\in\{-\infty,0,1,2,\dots\}$ be the supremum of the integers $n\ge0$ for which there is a chain $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_n$ of prime ideals all lying in $\operatorname{Supp}(N)$ ($-\infty$ when $\operatorname{Supp}(N)=\emptyset$, i.e. $N=0$; the same definition for any subset of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ in place of $\operatorname{Supp}(N)$). For elements $a_1,\dots,a_k\in R$ let $V(a_1,\dots,a_k)$ be the set of prime ideals of $R$ containing all $a_j$. Let $M\neq0$ be a finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] which is Cohen–Macaulay, i.e. $\operatorname{depth}(M)=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)$, where $\operatorname{depth}(M)=\operatorname{depth}_{\mathfrak m}(M)$ is the depth [def-weil-pbc-depth]; assume $d=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)$ is an integer $\ge1$, and let $f_1,\dots,f_d\in\mathfrak m$ be an $M$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] of length $d$. Let $g\in\mathfrak m$ be *good* with respect to $(M,f_1,\dots,f_d)$, that is, $\dim\bigl(\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(g,f_1,\dots,f_i)\bigr)=d-i-1$ for every $i=0,1,\dots,d-1$. Then (a) $g$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M$ (multiplication by $g$ on $M$ is injective), and (b) $M/gM$ is Cohen–Macaulay, $\operatorname{depth}(M/gM)=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M/gM)=d-1$, and $f_1,\dots,f_{d-1}$ is an $M/gM$-regular sequence (a maximal one, its length being $\operatorname{depth}(M/gM)$; for $d=1$ it is the empty sequence).

proof.text:
(Notation, facts used throughout, and the induction.) For an ideal $I=(a_1,\dots,a_k)$ write $M/(a_1,\dots,a_k)M$ for $M/IM$. (ii) By [lem-weil-pbc-support-quotient-ideal-module], $\operatorname{Supp}(N/(a_1,\dots,a_k)N)=\operatorname{Supp}(N)\cap V(a_1,\dots,a_k)$. (iii) For a finite $N

otin\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], but such $u$ is a unit of the local ring $R$. (iv) If $N
eq0$ is finite with $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(N)=e$ and $x_1,\dots,x_e\in\mathfrak m$ is an $N$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], then $\operatorname{depth}(N)\ge e$ by [def-weil-pbc-depth] (if $\mathfrak mN
eq N$ the supremum defining it runs over a set containing the length $e$ of this sequence; if $\mathfrak mN=N$ it is $\infty$), and $\operatorname{depth}(N)\le e$ by [lem-weil-pbc-depth-le-support-dimension]; so $\operatorname{depth}(N)=e=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(N)$: $N$ is Cohen–Macaulay and the sequence has maximal length. We prove by induction on $e\ge1$ the assertion $P(e)$: for every finite Cohen–Macaulay $R$-module $N
eq0$ with $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(N)=e$, every $N$-regular sequence $x_1,\dots,x_e\in\mathfrak m$ and every $y\in\mathfrak m$ good with respect to $(N,x_1,\dots,x_e)$, (a) and (b) hold for $(N,x_ ullet,y)$ in place of $(M,f_ ullet,g)$. Steps 2-4 prove $P(1)$, steps 5-8 prove $P(d)$ from $P(d-1)$ for $d\ge2$, written for $(M,f_ ullet,g)$ (Stacks: 'We prove the lemma by induction on $d$'). The case $d=0$ is excluded by the statement: see the split report (the source's lemma is false for $d=0$).

proof.text:
($d=1$: the kernel $K$ of $g$ and its support.) Let $d=1$ and $K=\{z\in M: gz=0\}$, an $R$-submodule of $M$; it is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite]. The goodness condition for $i=0$ says $\dim(\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(g))=0$. This set contains $\mathfrak m$ (step 1 (iii), and $g\in\mathfrak m$). It contains no other prime: if $\mathfrak p
eq\mathfrak m$ lay in it, then $\mathfrak p\subsetneq\mathfrak m$ ($R$ local) would be a chain of length $1$ in it. So $\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(g)=\{\mathfrak m\}$. Next $\operatorname{Supp}(K)\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(g)$: let $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Supp}(K)$, so some $z/s
eq0$ in $K_{\mathfrak p}$, hence $z/1
eq0$ ($s$ acts bijectively on $K_{\mathfrak p}$), i.e. $uz
eq0$ for every $u
otin\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]; this condition does not depend on whether $z$ is viewed in $K$ or in $M$, so $z/1
eq0$ in $M_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Supp}(M)$; and $g\in\mathfrak p$, for otherwise $u=g$ gives $gz=0$. Hence $\operatorname{Supp}(K)\subseteq\{\mathfrak m\}$ (Stacks: 'The kernel $K$ has support $\{\mathfrak m\}$ because by assumption $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(g)=0$').

proof.text:
($d=1$, (a): $K=0$.) Suppose $K
eq0$. By step 1 (iii) applied to the finite module $K$, $\mathfrak m\in\operatorname{Supp}(K)$, so $\operatorname{Supp}(K)=\{\mathfrak m\}$ by step 2 and $\mathfrak m$ is minimal in $\operatorname{Supp}(K)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-support-prime-associated] ($R$ Noetherian, $K$ finite) there is $z\in K$ with $\operatorname{Ann}_R(z)=\mathfrak m$; then $z
eq0$ (as $1
otin\mathfrak m$) and $f_1z=0$ (as $f_1\in\mathfrak m$). But $z\in M$ and $f_1$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M=M/(\emptyset)M$ by condition (1) of [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] for $i=1$: a contradiction. So $K=0$, i.e. $g$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M$. (The source concludes instead that $K$ has finite length, so the injective map $f_1:K	o K$ is onto, $f_1K=K$, and $K=0$ by Nakayama's Lemma 00DV; the argument here replaces those two facts by 05BV, already a Mathlib leaf in the DAG, and uses the same input: $\operatorname{Supp}(K)\subseteq\{\mathfrak m\}$ and $f_1$ injective on $K\subseteq M$.)

proof.text:
($d=1$, (b).) By step 1 (ii) and step 2, $\operatorname{Supp}(M/gM)=\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(g)=\{\mathfrak m\}$, which is nonempty, so $M/gM
eq0$ (its support would be empty otherwise), and $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M/gM)=0=d-1$. The empty sequence is an $M/gM$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] (condition (1) is empty, condition (2) is $M/gM
eq0$), of length $0$, in $\mathfrak m$. Now $\operatorname{depth}(M/gM)\ge0$ by [def-weil-pbc-depth] (its values lie in $\{0,1,2,\dots\}\cup\{\infty\}$) and $\operatorname{depth}(M/gM)\le\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M/gM)=0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-depth-le-support-dimension] ($M/gM
eq0$ finite), so $\operatorname{depth}(M/gM)=0=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M/gM)$ [def-weil-pbc-depth]: $M/gM$ is Cohen–Macaulay of depth $0=d-1$ with maximal regular sequence $f_1,\dots,f_{d-1}=\emptyset$. With step 3 this proves $P(1)$ (Stacks: 'Also, $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M/gM)=0$ and so $M/gM$ is Cohen-Macaulay of depth $0$').

proof.text: ($d\ge2$: the module $M'=M/f_1M$.) Let $d\ge2$ and assume $P(d-1)$. Put $M'=M/f_1M$, a finite $R$-module. By condition (1) of [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], $f_1\in\mathfrak m$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M$, so clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-support-dimension-quotient-element-equality] gives $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M')+1=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)=d$, i.e. $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M')=d-1\ge1$; in particular $\operatorname{Supp}(M')\neq\emptyset$ and $M'\neq0$. By step 1 (i), $M'/(f_2,\dots,f_i)M'=M/(f_1,\dots,f_i)M$ for $1\le i\le d$; so conditions (1) and (2) of [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] for $f_1,\dots,f_d$ on $M$, read for the indices $2,\dots,d$, say exactly that $f_2,\dots,f_d\in\mathfrak m$ is an $M'$-regular sequence, of length $d-1$. By step 1 (iv) (with $N=M'$, $e=d-1$), $M'$ is Cohen–Macaulay. So $M'$ is a nonzero finite Cohen–Macaulay module with $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M')=d-1$ and an $M'$-regular sequence $f_2,\dots,f_d\in\mathfrak m$ of length $d-1$, as $P(d-1)$ requires.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00N4 (lemma-good-element, line 24985), proof lines 24992-25015

proof.text: ($g$ is good with respect to $(M',f_2,\dots,f_d)$.) We need $\dim\bigl(\operatorname{Supp}(M')\cap V(g,f_2,\dots,f_{j+1})\bigr)=(d-1)-j-1$ for $j=0,\dots,d-2$. By step 1 (ii), $\operatorname{Supp}(M')=\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(f_1)$, and $V(f_1)\cap V(g,f_2,\dots,f_{j+1})=V(g,f_1,\dots,f_{j+1})$ (a prime contains all of $g,f_1,\dots,f_{j+1}$ iff it contains $f_1$ and the others). So the set in question is $\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(g,f_1,\dots,f_{i})$ with $i=j+1\in\{1,\dots,d-1\}$, whose dimension is $d-i-1=(d-1)-j-1$ by the goodness of $g$ with respect to $(M,f_1,\dots,f_d)$ (Stacks: 'Observe that $g$ is good for $(M/f_1M,f_2,\ldots,f_d)$, as is easily seen from the definition').

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00N4 (lemma-good-element, line 24985), proof lines 24992-25015

proof.text:
(Induction hypothesis and the swap; (a).) By steps 5 and 6, $P(d-1)$ applies to $(M',f_2,\dots,f_d,g)$: (a') $g$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M'=M/f_1M$, and (b') $M'/gM'=M/(f_1,g)M$ (step 1 (i)) is Cohen–Macaulay of depth $d-2$ and $f_2,\dots,f_{d-1}$ is an $M/(f_1,g)M$-regular sequence (empty if $d=2$); by condition (2) of [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] for it, $M/(f_1,g,f_2,\dots,f_{d-1})M
eq0$, hence $M/(f_1,g)M
eq0$ (it maps onto that module). So $f_1,g$ is an $M$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]: $f_1$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M$, $g$ one on $M/f_1M$, and $M/(f_1,g)M
eq0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-permutation-noetherian-local] ($R$ Noetherian local, $M$ finite) the permuted sequence $g,f_1$ is $M$-regular: $g$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M$, which is (a), and $f_1$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M/gM$ (Stacks: 'By Lemma 00LJ we see that $g,f_1$ is an $M$-regular sequence. Hence $g$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M$').

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00N4 (lemma-good-element, line 24985), proof lines 24992-25015

proof.text: ((b).) Put $\bar M=M/gM$. We check that $f_1,\dots,f_{d-1}\in\mathfrak m$ is $\bar M$-regular [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Condition (1) for $i=1$: $f_1$ is a nonzerodivisor on $\bar M$ (step 7). For $2\le i\le d-1$: by step 1 (i), $\bar M/(f_1,\dots,f_{i-1})\bar M=M/(g,f_1,\dots,f_{i-1})M=\bigl(M/(f_1,g)M\bigr)/(f_2,\dots,f_{i-1})\bigl(M/(f_1,g)M\bigr)$, on which $f_i$ is a nonzerodivisor by (b') of step 7 (index $i-1$ of the sequence $f_2,\dots,f_{d-1}$). Condition (2): $\bar M/(f_1,\dots,f_{d-1})\bar M=\bigl(M/(f_1,g)M\bigr)/(f_2,\dots,f_{d-1})\bigl(M/(f_1,g)M\bigr)\neq0$ by (b'). In particular $\bar M\neq0$. By step 1 (ii) and goodness for $i=0$, $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(\bar M)=\dim(\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(g))=d-1$. By step 1 (iv) with $N=\bar M$, $e=d-1$, $\operatorname{depth}(\bar M)=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(\bar M)=d-1$: $M/gM$ is Cohen–Macaulay with maximal regular sequence $f_1,\dots,f_{d-1}$. This proves $P(d)$ and completes the induction (Stacks: 'Hence $g$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M$ and $f_1,\ldots,f_{d-1}$ is an $M/gM$-regular sequence').

split_report.summary: Split following the proof of Stacks Algebra 00N4 (lemma-good-element, algebra.tex line 24985; tags 00N4, 00N3, 00LJ, 05BV, 00L3, 0B52, 00LK verified in tags/tags): induction on d, stated as P(e) over all (N, x_1..x_e, y) so that the induction hypothesis applies to M/f_1M; base case d = 1 via the kernel K of g; inductive step: M/f_1M is nonzero CM of dimension d-1 with regular sequence f_2..f_d (0B52 clause (2) leaf, 00LK), g is good for it, the induction hypothesis, then the swap f_1,g -> g,f_1 by 00LJ (leaf), and f_1..f_{d-1} is M/gM-regular, so M/gM is CM by 00LK. Statement corrected: d >= 1 added. SOURCE ERROR: for d = 0 the goodness condition is vacuous and (a) fails (R = k[x]_(x), M = R/(x), d = 0, g = x is good vacuously and kills M; also any field R = k, M = k, g = 0); the source says 'there is no case to which the lemma applies', which is wrong as written. The citer lem-weil-pbc-cm-module-good-element-nonzerodivisor applies the lemma only with d >= 1 (its step 3, after its step 1 shows d >= 1) and with d >= 2 (its step 7), so it is unaffected. Departure inside the node (below the unit): in the case d = 1 the source shows K has finite length (00L5), so f_1K = K and Nakayama gives K = 0; here K = 0 follows from Supp K = {m} and 05BV (m is then associated to K, so f_1 in m kills a nonzero element of M), using the existing Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-minimal-support-prime-associated instead of two new nodes (00L5 is not in Mathlib). Written out where the source is silent: m in Supp of a nonzero finite module; Supp M ∩ V(g) = {m} for d = 1; Supp K ⊆ Supp M ∩ V(g); finiteness of K; that M/f_1M is CM of dimension d-1 and M/gM nonzero; the identification of iterated quotients; that M/(f_1,g)M ≠ 0. No new nodes; every node cited is of unit sk-thm-p1 or a Mathlib leaf. What the citer uses ((a), (b) with depth(M/gM) = dim Supp(M/gM) = d-1) is proved.
